verses.text: When King Hezekiah heard what had happened, he tore his clothes, wrapped himself in sackcloth, and went into the LORD's house.
He sent Eliakim, who ran the household, Shebna the scribe, and the senior priests to Isaiah the prophet, Amoz's son. They all wore sackcloth.
They told him, “Hezekiah says, ‘Today we're in trouble. We're being rebuked and rejected. It's like the babies are ready to be born, but there's no strength left to deliver them.

Maybe the LORD your God will hear what Rabshakeh said. His master, the king of Assyria, sent him to throw insults at the living God. Maybe the LORD your God will call him to account for what he's heard. So pray for the few of us who are left.’”
That's how King Hezekiah's servants came to Isaiah.
Isaiah told them, “Tell your master, ‘The LORD says, “Don't be scared of what you heard. The king of Assyria's servants were insulting me with those words.
Look, I'll put a spirit in him. He'll hear news and go back to his own land, and I'll make him fall by the sword there.”’”
Rabshakeh went back and found the king of Assyria fighting Libnah. He'd heard the king had left Lachish.
The king heard news about Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia: “He's come out to fight you.” When he heard that, he sent messengers to Hezekiah.
“Tell Hezekiah king of Judah, ‘Don't let the God you trust fool you by saying, “Jerusalem won't be handed over to the king of Assyria.”
You've heard what Assyria's kings have done to all those lands. They wiped them out. You think you'll get away?
Did the gods of the nations my ancestors destroyed save them? What about Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar?
Where's the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of Sepharvaim, or the kings of Hena and Ivvah?’”
Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the LORD's house and spread the letter out in front of the LORD.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD.
“LORD of Armies, God of Israel, you sit enthroned among the cherubim. You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.
Lean in and listen, LORD. Open your eyes and look. Hear everything Sennacherib sent to say against the living God.
It's true, LORD. The kings of Assyria have destroyed all those nations and their lands.
They threw their gods into the fire. Those were no gods, just wood and stone made by human hands. That's how they could destroy them.
So now, LORD our God, save us from his hand. Let all the kingdoms on earth know that you alone are the LORD.”
Then Isaiah, Amoz's son, sent Hezekiah this message. “The LORD, Israel's God, says, ‘You've prayed to me about Sennacherib, king of Assyria.
Here's what the LORD has said about him. The virgin daughter of Zion looks down on you and laughs. Daughter Jerusalem shakes her head at you.
Who were you defying and insulting? Who did you raise your voice at and look down on so proudly? The Holy One of Israel.

You sent your servants to defy the Lord, saying, “With all my chariots I've climbed the highest mountains and reached deep into Lebanon. I'll cut down its tallest cedars and its finest cypresses. I'll go to its farthest heights, into the forest of its fertile land.
I dug wells and drank the water, and I'll dry up every river in Egypt with the soles of my feet.”
Haven't you heard? I did this long ago. I planned it in ancient times. Now I've brought it about, so you'd turn those fortified cities into heaps of rubble.
That's why the people there had no strength. They were scared and humiliated. They were like grass in a field, like green shoots, like grass on the roof or a field before the crop comes up.
But I know when you sit down, when you go out and come in, and how you rage against me.
Your rage and arrogance have reached my ears. So I'll put my hook in your nose and my bridle between your lips and turn you back the way you came.
Here's your sign, Hezekiah. This year you'll eat what grows on its own. The next year you'll eat what grows from that. In the third year, plant and harvest. Plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
The survivors of Judah's household will put roots down again and grow fruit up above.
A remnant will come out of Jerusalem, and survivors will escape from Mount Zion. The LORD of Armies will make it happen with his own zeal.’
So here's what the LORD says about the king of Assyria. ‘He won't enter this city or shoot an arrow into it. He won't come up against it with a shield or build a siege mound against it.
He'll go back the way he came. He won't enter this city,’ says the LORD.
‘I'll defend this city and save it for my own sake and for my servant David's sake.’”
Then the LORD's angel went out and struck down 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp. When people got up early in the morning, all they saw were dead bodies.
So Sennacherib, king of Assyria, left, went back to Nineveh, and stayed there.

While he was worshiping in the temple of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esar Haddon became king in his place.
